level1.text: The wavelength of the red light of a helium–neon laser is $633\,\text{nm}$. Calculate the energy of one laser photon in electronvolts ($h = 6.626 \cdot 10^{-34}\,\text{J}\,\text{s}$, $c = 2.998 \cdot 10^{8}\,\text{m/s}$, $1\,\text{eV} = 1.602 \cdot 10^{-19}\,\text{J}$).

Optical fibre links use laser diodes whose light has the wavelength $1550\,\text{nm}$. Calculate the energy of one photon in electronvolts ($h = 6.626 \cdot 10^{-34}\,\text{J}\,\text{s}$, $c = 2.998 \cdot 10^{8}\,\text{m/s}$, $1\,\text{eV} = 1.602 \cdot 10^{-19}\,\text{J}$).

The energy difference of the levels of the laser transition of a ruby laser is $1.79\,\text{eV}$. Calculate the wavelength of the laser light in nanometres ($h = 6.626 \cdot 10^{-34}\,\text{J}\,\text{s}$, $c = 2.998 \cdot 10^{8}\,\text{m/s}$, $1\,\text{eV} = 1.602 \cdot 10^{-19}\,\text{J}$).

The energy of one light pulse of a pulsed laser is $3.0\,\text{mJ}$, and the wavelength of the light is $1064\,\text{nm}$. How many photons are there in the pulse ($h = 6.626 \cdot 10^{-34}\,\text{J}\,\text{s}$, $c = 2.998 \cdot 10^{8}\,\text{m/s}$)?

A laser emits $4.0 \cdot 10^{15}$ photons per second, and the energy of each photon is $2.33\,\text{eV}$. Calculate the power of the laser in milliwatts ($1\,\text{eV} = 1.602 \cdot 10^{-19}\,\text{J}$).

level2.text: A neodymium laser is pumped with a laser diode whose light has the wavelength $808\,\text{nm}$, and the laser emits light with the wavelength $1064\,\text{nm}$. Each pump photon produces at most one laser photon. At most what percentage of the energy of a pump photon can end up as the energy of a laser photon?

The wavelength of a red laser pointer is $650\,\text{nm}$ and that of a violet one $405\,\text{nm}$. The power of both is $5.0\,\text{mW}$. How many times more photons per second does the red laser pointer emit than the violet one?

A quantum dot with a diameter of $6.0\,\text{nm}$ emits light with the wavelength $620\,\text{nm}$. The photon energy of a smaller quantum dot made of the same material is $0.35\,\text{eV}$ greater. Calculate the wavelength of the light of the smaller dot in nanometres ($h = 6.626 \cdot 10^{-34}\,\text{J}\,\text{s}$, $c = 2.998 \cdot 10^{8}\,\text{m/s}$, $1\,\text{eV} = 1.602 \cdot 10^{-19}\,\text{J}$).

One pulse of a pulsed laser has $2.7 \cdot 10^{17}$ photons with the wavelength $1064\,\text{nm}$. The duration of the pulse is $10\,\text{ns}$. Calculate the average power of the pulse in megawatts ($h = 6.626 \cdot 10^{-34}\,\text{J}\,\text{s}$, $c = 2.998 \cdot 10^{8}\,\text{m/s}$).

level3.text:
The rod of a ruby laser has $1.0 \cdot 10^{19}$ chromium ions, and the laser transition ends in the ground state. The wavelength of the green light of the pump lamp is $550\,\text{nm}$, and each absorbed pump photon lifts one ion to the upper laser level.

Estimate how much energy of the pump light the ions must absorb at least for a population inversion to appear. Assume that the ions do not have time to decay during the pumping. Give the answer in joules ($h = 6.626 \cdot 10^{-34}\,\text{J}\,\text{s}$, $c = 2.998 \cdot 10^{8}\,\text{m/s}$).

In a green laser pointer, the light of an infrared laser diode ($808\,\text{nm}$, power $1.0\,\text{W}$) pumps a crystal that emits laser light with the wavelength $1064\,\text{nm}$. A second crystal always combines two $1064\,\text{nm}$ photons into one $532\,\text{nm}$ photon. At most how many green photons per second can the laser pointer emit, when each pump photon produces at most one $1064\,\text{nm}$ photon ($h = 6.626 \cdot 10^{-34}\,\text{J}\,\text{s}$, $c = 2.998 \cdot 10^{8}\,\text{m/s}$)?

The energy difference of the two states of a superconducting qubit corresponds to a photon with the frequency $5.0\,\text{GHz}$. How many times greater is the energy of a photon of red light ($650\,\text{nm}$) than the energy difference of the states of the qubit ($c = 2.998 \cdot 10^{8}\,\text{m/s}$)?
